Class CheckValve

neqsim.process.equipment.valve.CheckValve
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Runnable, AutoSizeable, TransientStateParticipant<ThrottlingValve.TransientState>, CapacityConstrainedEquipment, ProcessEquipmentInterface, TwoPortInterface, ValveInterface, ProcessElementInterface, SimulationInterface, NamedInterface, LegacyLoadRepairable
public class CheckValve extends ThrottlingValve
Check valve (non-return valve) that prevents reverse flow.

CheckValve is a self-actuating valve that opens when forward differential pressure exceeds the cracking pressure, and closes when flow reverses or stops. It is essential for protecting equipment like pumps and compressors from reverse flow damage.

Key features:

  • Automatic operation based on differential pressure
  • Configurable cracking pressure (minimum ΔP to open)
  • Prevents backflow in piping systems
  • Zero leakage when closed (ideal model)
  • Minimal pressure drop when fully open

Common applications:

  • Pump discharge protection
  • Compressor discharge protection
  • Parallel equipment isolation
  • Gravity drainage systems
  • Preventing siphoning

Example usage: 

 CheckValve checkValve = new CheckValve("CV-101", pumpDischargeStream);
 checkValve.setCrackingPressure(0.2); // Opens at 0.2 bar differential
 checkValve.setCv(250.0); // Flow coefficient when fully open
 checkValve.run();

 boolean forwardFlowAvailable = checkValve.isOpen();

    • run

      public void run(UUID id)
      Executes the ideal passive pressure gate through the native UUID path.

      The actual downstream stream supplies the absolute pressure boundary, including after a zero-flow calculation. The cracking pressure is an opening threshold, not an additional vendor pressure-loss correlation. This model does not resolve disc motion, slam, leakage or reverse rotation.

      Specified by:
      run in interface SimulationInterface
      Overrides:
      run in class ThrottlingValve
      Parameters:
      id - calculation identifier

    • calculateMolarFlow

      public double calculateMolarFlow()
      Queries native hydraulic capacity with the same passive opening gate and no flash.

      Valid inlet composition and phase state are retained in a detached normalized intensive workspace. No stream is flashed. This query may update the ideal seat state but does not withdraw mass, advance time or stamp a physical-step identifier. A subsequent native run is required to publish actual port flows and enthalpy.

      Overrides:
      calculateMolarFlow in class ThrottlingValve
      Returns:
      forward capacity in mole/sec, or exact zero below the opening threshold

    • isZeroFlowPressureBoundaryEnabled

      protected boolean isZeroFlowPressureBoundaryEnabled()
      Allows a reviewed pressure-boundary subclass to calculate native Cv flow from zero specified throughput.

      The default is false: an ordinary initially dry valve remains dry. An opt-in model treats finite nonnegative negligible throughput with usable composition as an intensive-property workspace only; actual computed flow replaces it, or both ports return to exact zero on closure, absent forward pressure difference or failure. This does not supply an inventory.

      Overrides:
      isZeroFlowPressureBoundaryEnabled in class ThrottlingValve
      Returns:
      true only for an explicitly pressure-driven boundary model
